purpose: Actual-read official primary source packet for aw079–083 titles and effective bodies.

sources.title: ITF Coaching and Sports Science Review - Contact Point & Timing
sources.actualReadClaim: ITF CSSR studies identify visual delay on slow balls (<40km/h) and specify impact zone forward momentum transfer.
sources.limits: Coaching biomechanics principles; individual player height and grip affect exact contact height.

sources.title: USTA Tennis Skills & Drills: Groundstroke Footwork
sources.actualReadClaim: USTA coaching curricula emphasize step-in footwork and maintaining racquet head acceleration through contact.
sources.limits: Standard drill progressions; not a universal timing prescription for every incoming trajectory.

sources.title: ITF Rules of Tennis 2026 - Rule 24 Player Loses Point & Net Dimensions
sources.actualReadClaim: ITF Rule 24 specifies point loss conditions, net height standard of 0.914m at center, and boundary dimensions.
sources.limits: Official governing match rule; does not prescribe individual tactical choices.

sources.title: USTA Player Development: High Ball & Strike Zone Management
sources.actualReadClaim: USTA development guides define optimal strike zone between hip and chest and delineate rising versus drop-back tactics.
sources.limits: Biomechanic development framework; surface friction alters bounce speed and height.

sources.title: ITF Rules of Tennis 2026 - Rule 29 Continuous Play & Intervals
sources.actualReadClaim: ITF Rule 29 mandates continuous play with a maximum of 25 seconds between points.
sources.limits: Match rule timing ceiling; umpire discretion governs enforcement nuances.

sources.title: USTA Adult League Guidelines - Pace of Play and Partner Signaling
sources.actualReadClaim: USTA Adult League rules require steady pace of play and brief concise non-verbal/verbal signaling between partners.
sources.limits: League regulation framework; non-officiated recreational matches adapt by mutual agreement.

sources.title: ITF Rules of Tennis 2026 - Rules 16-19 Service Delivery & Faults
sources.actualReadClaim: ITF Rules 16-19 govern legal service delivery, toss restrictions, and foot fault/service fault definitions.
sources.limits: Rule definitions; technical mechanics and consistency drills are training applications.

sources.title: USTA Performance Metrics - Serve Consistency & Toss Tracking
sources.actualReadClaim: USTA coaching analytics isolate toss location variance and second-serve racquet speed deceleration as primary double fault drivers.
sources.limits: Self-tracking protocol; wind and environmental factors introduce toss deviation.

sources.title: USTA Warrior Doubles Strategy - Lob Defense Formations
sources.actualReadClaim: USTA Warrior Doubles outlines net player depth adjustment and baseline partner diagonal cover protocols against offensive lobs.
sources.limits: Recreational and club doubles tactics; mobility differences between partners require customized depth.

sources.title: ITF Coaching Doubles Tactics - Overhead and Recovery Movement
sources.actualReadClaim: ITF coaching guides advise against dangerous backpedaling and recommend lateral turn-and-run recovery for overhead defense.
sources.limits: Safety and biomechanics guidance; court surface traction affects safe retreat speed.
